title: Umklapp-enhanced high-$T_c$ topological superconductivity mediated by magnons in $p$-wave magnets
summary: We show that magnon exchange can induce nodal topological superconductivity in a microscopic model of a $p$-wave magnet. Solving the weak-coupling multiband gap equation for itinerant electrons exchange-coupled to localized spins, we find a nodal $p$-wave gap and a critical temperature that rises sharply as the Fermi surface approaches the magnetic Brillouin-zone boundary. In this regime, small-reduced-momentum magnons can scatter electrons between Fermi-surface segments on opposite sides of the zone. These Umklapp processes enhance pairing because the contributions from different sites in the magnetic unit cell cancel less in their electron-magnon vertices than in those for ordinary scattering at comparable reduced momenta. Momentum-resolved winding numbers predict zero-energy Majorana flat bands at symmetry-preserving edges where the bulk nodes project to distinct momenta.

title: First order vortex-unbinding transition in 2D topological superconductors
summary: We study the fate of the Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT) transition in a two-dimensional topological superconductor whose vortex cores each host an isolated Majorana zero mode, energetically well separated from the bulk gap and other bound states of the vortex. When the Majorana localization length $ξ_F$ exceeds the vortex core size $ξ$, nearby vortices acquire an additional short-range attractive channel from Majorana hybridization, modifying the vortex-antivortex interaction at short distances and generating a metastable minimum in the two-vortex free energy above the nominal $T_{BKT}$. We construct an effective field theory for the resulting dilute vortex gas, coupling the ordinary BKT phase field to an additional field encoding the Majorana-mediated interaction, and show, using renormalization-group and instanton methods, that this hybridization can drive the transition first order, with the metastable phase decaying at an exponentially small rate. We propose an array of Josephson-coupled $p+ip$ superconducting islands as a microscopic platform realizing the required hierarchy of scales. Finally, we discuss experimental signatures of this first-order transition, in particular a hysteresis loop whose width is set by the coexistence window.

title: Magnetic order in Tb and Dy substituted La3Ni2O7 and effects of high-pressure high-temperature O2 annealing
summary: To study the influence of magnetic lanthanide (Ln) substituents on La3Ni2O7, polycrystalline samples of La3-xLnxNi2O7 (Ln = Pr, Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, Tm, and Yb) were synthesized and characterized by electrical transport, magnetization, and x-ray and neutron powder diffraction before and after high-pressure high-temperature oxygen annealing. The annealing process led to the formation of La3Ni2O7 polymorphs and more metallic-like temperature dependence of the electrical resistance while changing the density-wave transition temperature only slightly. For unannealed La2.7Tb0.3Ni2O7 and La2.7Dy0.3Ni2O7, distinct features in the magnetic susceptibility and additional magnetic peaks in neutron diffraction patterns indicate that both samples develop long-range magnetic order below ~13 and 11 K, respectively. The magnetic signatures were strongly suppressed following oxygen annealing, suggesting a possible association with the accompanying structural modifications. These behaviors distinguish Tb and Dy from Pr, Nd, and Sm substituents which do not introduce magnetic ordering in the system, establishing La3-xTbxNi2O7 and La3-xDyxNi2O7 as promising platforms for exploring the interplay between magnetic order and pressure-induced superconductivity in La3Ni2O7.

title: Generalized Critical-State Analysis of Local Field Screening in High-Pressure Yttrium Polyhydride
summary: We resolve the long-standing controversy over the interpretation of magnetic-flux expulsion in high-pressure superhydrides by measuring the local magnetic field adjacent to yttrium polyhydride at 171 GPa and 4.1 K with a $^{57}$Fe Mössbauer sensor. Nuclear forward scattering tracks the local induction $B_{\rm sensor}(B_a)$, which nearly merges with the normal-state line near 1.5 T. Rather than assuming a constant-current Bean state, we solve the critical-state problem for the actual thin-disk geometry using the Shantsev--Clem--Sanchez method and compare generalized field-dependent critical-state models. Both the Kim and exponential laws reproduce the measured virgin branch, whereas the constant-$J_c$ Bean model fails. The corresponding zero-field critical-current densities, $(4.38\pm1.48)\times10^{11}$ and $(2.45\pm0.22)\times10^{11}$ A/m$^2$, respectively, are consistent in order of magnitude with transport estimates for granular YH$_6$. These results establish that the observed flux expulsion is a pinned critical state, not the equilibrium Meissner effect, and demonstrate a general methodology for probing local superconductivity under extreme conditions.

title: Chiral Phonons Protected by Symmetry in a Strongly Anharmonic Helical Material
summary: How chiral phonons survive anharmonic phonon-phonon interactions, which underpin lattice dynamics at finite temperature, remains poorly understood. Using an ab initio many-body approach, we study crystalline tellurium (Te), a strongly anharmonic helical crystal. We show that rotational symmetries in Te impose pseudoangular momentum selection rules on phonon-phonon interactions, restricting mode mixing and scattering at rotationally invariant symmetry points in the Brillouin zone. These symmetries protect the circular polarization of vibrational modes at finite temperature but not their lifetimes such that the dynamic chirality of handed vibrational modes persists to 600 K, even as lifetimes drop sharply. We find that the temperature-dependence of angular momentum generated by a thermal gradient is governed by lifetimes rather than chirality, decreasing by two orders of magnitude between 10 and 600 K.

title: Exact Fractional Chern Insulators from Hubbard Interactions
summary: Laughlin's wavefunction and its parent interaction, Haldane's pseudopotential, underpin our analytic understanding of fractional quantum Hall effect. They are an exact pair in the sense that the wavefunction is the unique, zero-energy ground state of its frustration-free parent Hamiltonian. In this work, we propose exact pairs of many-body wavefunctions for fractional Chern insulators in tight binding models with onsite Hubbard interactions as their parents. The key to our construction is introduction of a Landau-dual Chern band, a multi-orbital Chern band obtained from directly sampling the spin-$s$ Dirac Landau level on a Bravais lattice. The exact many-body wavefunctions are given, analytically, in terms of the matrix coordinate $X+iY+J$, where $(X,Y)$ are the lattice coordinates and $J$ is a nilpotent matrix in spin space. The constructed exact pairs cover the fractional Chern states of the Laughlin, the Read-Rezayi, and the Halperin series. Our results prove that FCI ground states exist beyond ideal bands.

title: Comparative First-Principles Study of the Physical Properties, Phonon-Mediated Superconductivity and Functional Potential of Technetium-Based Binary Borides TcB2, Tc2B and Tc3B
summary: Phonon-mediated superconductivity in binary transition-metal borides reflects a balance between the metal d-states, metal-boron bonding, and the lattice vibrations that couple to them. Here, we compare P6/mmm TcB2 at 20 GPa with I4/mcm Tc2B and P4/mmm Tc3B at 0 GPa within a first-principles framework. Their mechanical responses differ appreciably: TcB2 is the most rigid under its compressed condition, Tc2B shows the strongest tendency toward ductility, and Tc3B falls between the two. Despite these differences, all three phases remain metallic. The states at the Fermi level are dominated by Tc-4d character, although the extent of Tc-d/B-p mixing varies from one compound to another. Charge redistribution is more directional and B-centered in TcB2, but more delocalized around the Tc network in Tc2B and Tc3B. Inclusion of spin-orbit coupling leaves all three compounds metallic. The optical response remains metallic and electric field polarization dependent, with substantial visible reflectivity and strong ultraviolet absorption. Low-frequency Tc rich vibrations dominate the electron-phonon coupling (EPC). With μ* = 0.10, the Tc values of TcB2, Tc2B, and Tc3B are 24.92, 11.07, and 15.12 K, respectively. Although Tc3B exhibits a higher electronic density of states at the Fermi level, N(EF), TcB2 couples most strongly to EPC-active low-frequency modes, showing that the superconducting hierarchy depends on electronic-phonon matching rather than DOS magnitude alone.

title: A plane-wave auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo study of silicon point defects
summary: Accurately predicting the energetics of point defects remains a formidable challenge in computational materials science. For the tetrahedral silicon self-interstitial, for example, previous periodic coupled-cluster [CCSD(T)] and diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) calculations disagree by about 1.2 eV. Here, we present formation energies of silicon self-interstitials and vacancies using auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) in a plane-wave basis formulated within the projector-augmented wave framework, and compare them with the random-phase approximation (RPA) and CCSD(T). Using 16- and 64-atom cells, we demonstrate that an RPA-based correction effectively removes the two-body finite-size errors that remain after twist averaging in AFQMC for bulk silicon and for the dumbbell and hexagonal self-interstitials. With this correction, we obtain formation energies of 4.4 eV and 4.6 eV for these two self-interstitials in 16-atom cells, in good agreement with DMC and transcorrelated coupled-cluster results. For the tetrahedral interstitial and the Jahn--Teller-distorted vacancy, 16-atom cells are too small to obtain realistic formation energies; in 64-atom cells, we obtain 5.7 eV and 5.2 eV, respectively. With identical setups in 16-atom cells, CCSD(T) yields systematically lower formation energies than AFQMC, with the largest difference, 250 meV, for the tetrahedral interstitial. Our results indicate that the earlier overestimation of CCSD(T) for the tetrahedral interstitial stems from the finite-size treatment in the coupled-cluster workflow rather than from multi-configurational character of the defect.

title: Anyon Coherent States in Fractional Chern Insulators
comment: 6 pages and 3 figures in the main text; 27 pages and 13 figures in total, including appendices
summary: In fractional quantum Hall (FQH) systems, coherent anyonic excitations are the natural entities for describing anyon dynamics, their interactions, and braiding, yet no general expression for their wavefunctions is known beyond Laughlin's quasiholes. We introduce a systematic, operator-based construction of maximally-localized wavefunctions of anyons of either charge in FQH states and fractional Chern insulators, including those in non-ideal, non-vortexable bands. We find that these wavefunctions describe coherent quasiparticles: zero modes of local annihilation operators that saturate projected-density uncertainty bounds. These coherent states owe their existence to a nontrivial topology of the anyon band, with the winding of their Bloch coefficients encoding an anyon band's Chern number. As such, their guiding centers exist anywhere within the lattice, and their mutual overlaps decay as Gaussians determined by the effective magnetic length of the anyon band.

title: Ab-initio study of magnetic interaction in RNiO2: role of rare-earth size and epitaxial strain
summary: In this paper we present a systematic first-principles investigation of the structure and nearest-neighbor magnetic exchange interactions in the infinite-layer RNiO2 thin-film series (R = La-Lu), under the constrain of different substrates. Density functional theory calculations are first employed to optimize the crystal structures, while CAS+DDCI correlated wave-function calculations were used for the determination of the magnetic exchanges. This methodology allows to obtain magnetic interactions in good agreement with RIXS experimental estimations. In the pristine case, our results confirm that the structure of RNiO2 (except for R = La and Ce) adopts the I4/mcm space group, characterized by an out-of-plane rotation of the NiO4 plaquettes. This result remains valid under substrate constrains, even if compressive strain reduces the amplitude of the rotational distortion and leads to an enhancement of the magnetic exchange interaction relative to the pristine structures. The latter are found to depend sensitively on both the rare-earth ionic radius and the applied epitaxial strain. These results highlight the role of structural distortions and substrate-induced strain in tuning magnetic interactions in infinite-layer nickelates.

title: Machine Learning-Driven High-Throughput Screening of Equimolar and Non-Equimolar High-Entropy Carbides
summary: Search for optimal compositions among high-entropy ceramics are challenging due to large composition space, which are unable to test either experimentally or by \textit{ab initio} calculations. Here we present a high-throughput screening for equimolar and non-equimolar high-entropy carbides (HEC) among group IVB and VB transition metals (Ti, Zr, Hf, V, Nb and Ta). Large Atomistic Model MACE, and deep learning based interatomic potential DeePMD trained on \textit{ab initio}-based dataset of structures are used to effectively screen over the thousands of potential non-equimolar compositions among high-entropy carbides of Ti, Zr, Hf, V, Nb and Ta transition metals. A set of both equimolar and non-equimolar HECs are predicted to be stable in order to further synthesize those compositions based on the predictions.

title: Quantum many-body scars and zero modes in the spin-1 Kitaev chain
summary: We study the spin-1 Kitaev chain and, by analyzing its Hilbert-space connectivity in the Cartesian basis, show that it hosts an exponentially large number of exact zero-energy modes protected by chiral symmetry. For even-length periodic chains, their count is lower-bounded by the Jacobsthal number $(2^{L+1}+1)/3$, where $L$ is the chain length. We then construct an exponentially large number ($2^{L/2}$) of zero modes with an analytic expression that have a maximally mixed density matrix for a contiguous bipartition using the operator-state mapping. We further identify an embedded tight-binding structure governing defect dynamics that supports PXP-like quantum many-body scars (QMBS) in multiple sectors previously not reported. The associated forward-scattering approximation (FSA) Hamiltonian takes a universal form across the scarred sectors studied. A simple physical picture of defects propagating between walls provides an intuitive description of these dynamics and a structural guide to identifying sectors with fidelity revivals, while its limitations point to additional scarring mechanisms.

title: Quantum Metric Control of Topological Superconductivity and Incommensurate Charge Density Wave in an Interacting Lieb-Kitaev Chain Model
summary: We study an interacting spinless Lieb-Kitaev chain model in the nearly flat-band regime, motivated by the recent observation that Majorana zero modes in the noninteracting Lieb-Kitaev system inherit two decay modes: an ordinary Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) length and a longer geometric length controlled by the quantum metric. By tuning both the interaction strength and quantum metric, we identify a topological superconducting (TSC) phase, an incommensurate charge-density-wave (ICDW)phase, and a commensurate charge-density-wave (CDW) phase. Inside the TSC phase, the QML is enhanced when increasing the interactions. In the ICDW phase, the interactions are modulated by quantum metric to generate an effective chemical potential, leading to a discontinuous incommensurate-to-commensurate (IC-C) transition. We verify these phases and conclusions using low energy effective theory and density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations.

title: A Symmetry-Stratified Framework for Phase Transitions: Thermodynamic States, Critical Dynamics, and Spectral Mechanical Signatures
summary: Structural symmetry, thermodynamic phase stability, and elastic-wave response provide related but distinct descriptions of a transforming solid. We formulate a symmetry-stratified framework that connects these descriptions through a finite-dimensional internal state and a parent-invariant free energy. Stabilizers classify structural states, whereas free-energy comparisons and stability conditions determine equilibrium branches and dissipative evolution. Equivariance ensures that the frozen elastic tangent inherits the structural stabilizer. Equality requires additional identifiability conditions. Little-group representations and degenerate perturbation theory then determine whether an acoustic doublet splits and the first nonzero splitting order $p$. On a selected continuous branch with order-parameter exponent $β$, a regular, observable acoustic gap scales as $|t|^{pβ}$, provided critical self-energies and structural relaxation do not dominate the measurement. Explicit tensorial and cubic-to-tetragonal realizations yield linear and quadratic splitting channels, together with directionally protected degeneracies. Separate numerical benchmarks examine free-energy reconstruction, coexistence, elastic compatibility, finite-temperature spectra, and controlled critical readouts. Reanalysis of NiTi measurements illustrates effective elastic degeneracy, thermal-history dependence, and the predictive value of independently measured phase fractions. Most importantly, the framework identifies the constitutive and measurement assumptions required to infer structural changes from mechanical spectra.

title: The phase diagram of fluid hydrogen near melting from machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on quantum Monte Carlo
summary: Dissociation of molecular hydrogen increasing temperature or pressure may either occur gradually or abruptly, via a phase transition. Despite considerable experimental and theoretical efforts, the phase diagram of dense hydrogen at temperatures above solid melting is not precisely known. Here, we perform classical and quantum Path Integral molecular dynamics simulations of dense hydrogen using two machine-learned interatomic potentials both trained on quantum Monte Carlo energies and forces. The resulting phase diagram is constructed using state-of-the-art techniques. Both models show a first-order phase transition from the molecular to the atomic liquid terminating in critical points whose locations were determined using finite-size scaling techniques. Triple points, located at the highest temperature of the melting curve, are found at the intersection of the liquid-liquid lines with the melting curve and should lead to clear signatures in ramp compression experiments.

title: Single-Crystal Growth, Structure, and Physical Properties of Yb2MoO6
summary: Rare-earth molybdates are functional oxides of considerable interest because their structural and chemical flexibility enables diverse magnetic, electronic, and optical behavior. Here, millimeter-sized single crystals of $Yb_2MoO_6$ are synthesized, their crystal structure determined and physical properties investigated. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirms the formation of $Yb_2MoO_6$ and yielded lattice parameters of $a = 16.228(2)$ $\mathring{A}$, $b = 10.901(3)$ $\mathring{A}$, and $c = 5.286(2)$ $\mathring{A}$, in good agreement with previously reported neutron powder diffraction data. Scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive spectroscopy show a Yb:Mo ratio close to the expected 2:1 stoichiometry. Optical measurements based on diffuse-reflectance spectra and Tauc analysis yield an estimated optical gap of $\sim 3.28$ eV under the direct-allowed transition assumption. Magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal Curie-Weiss-like paramagnetic behavior, with an effective magnetic moment of $μ_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx 4.2μ_B$ per Yb and an apparent Weiss temperature of $θ\approx -65.7$ K, consistent with possible antiferromagnetic interactions or correlations, with no clear magnetic-ordering transition observed down to 10 K. These results establish the growth of $Yb_2MoO_6$ single crystals and provide initial insight into their structural, optical, and magnetic properties.

title: Canted antiferromagnetism and spin-flop transition in honeycomb $α$-Na$_2$PrO$_3$ revealed by angle-dependent torque magnetometry up to 35 T
summary: We report angle-dependent piezocantilever torque measurements on single crystals of the honeycomb magnet $α$-Na$_2$PrO$_3$, proposed to display unconventional magnetism stabilized by anisotropic exchange interactions between spin-orbit entangled, pseudospin 1/2 Pr$^{4+}$ magnetic moments. Previous powder susceptibility observed signatures of a transition at low temperatures to antiferromagnetic order with a weak ferromagnetic moment. From the torque angular dependence in three orthogonal crystallographic planes, we infer a zero-field canted antiferromagnetic structure, with moments almost normal to the honeycomb layers, but weakly canted such as to give rise to a spontaneous magnetization along the in-plane monoclinic $a$-axis, with two magnetic domains related by time reversal. Sharp jumps in the torque angular dependence when the field projection along $a$ changes sign are interpreted as field-induced switching between the two degenerate domains with oppositely aligned ferromagnetic moments. We propose a minimal spin Hamiltonian including easy-axis exchange anisotropy and symmetry-allowed Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) couplings, for which mean-field calculations reproduce the main features of the observed angle-dependent torque. Torque measurements up to 35 T applied almost normal to the layers observe a strong anomaly attributed to proximity to the field-induced spin-flop transition predicted for the above Hamiltonian. We contrast the predicted magnetic phase diagrams for magnetic fields in different orthogonal crystallographic planes normal to the honeycomb layers and discuss how DM interactions convert some transitions into smooth crossovers and stabilize a phase boundary line connecting the spin-flop transition in field normal to the layers to magnetization saturation for in-plane field normal to $a$; such a phase boundary line does not exist in the absence of DM interactions.

title: Molecular engineering for crack-free transfer of single-crystalline oxide membranes onto silicon
summary: Heterogeneous integration of single-crystalline complex oxides with silicon offers a route to incorporating their functionalities into next-generation microelectronics. Released from their growth substrates, freestanding oxide membranes enable this integration. However, cracks, wrinkles, and fragmentation during release and transfer limit membrane size and quality. Here, we present an interfacial energy-controlled release strategy that enables crack-free, single-crystalline freestanding oxide membranes with centimeter-scale lateral dimensions. Using SrTiO3 as a model system, time-resolved release studies identify water-induced blistering at the membrane-support interface during prolonged water exposure as the origin of membrane cracking. Lowering the molecular weight of the poly(propylene carbonate) support through polymer deconstruction increases its polarity and surface energy, suppresses interfacial blistering, and reduces organic residue after support removal. The resulting SrTiO3 membranes exhibit optical properties comparable to those of bulk single crystals. We extend this approach to the metallic ferromagnet La0.7Sr0.3MnO3, obtaining crack-free membranes on Si that preserve ferromagnetism and metallicity.

title: Learning Spin Hamiltonians from Interacting Magnon Spectra
summary: A neural network that learns an inverse map inherits the approximations of the forward solver used to generate its training data. We demonstrate this in the inference of spin Hamiltonians from synthetic neutron-scattering spectra and show how a fast many-body solver can overcome the limitation of linear spin-wave theory (LSWT). We consider a family of anisotropic triangular-lattice spin Hamiltonians at fields just above saturation, where magnon interactions shift and broaden the spectrum in ways that LSWT cannot capture. Using the truncated Hilbert-space ladder (THL) method, we compute the dynamical spin structure factor (DSSF) nonperturbatively within the one- and two-magnon space. THL is fast enough to generate large training sets of DSSF spectra, enabling us to train neural networks that accurately predict Hamiltonian parameters. By empirically benchmarking several neural-network architectures, we find that a one-dimensional convolutional network performs best. A learned forward decoder then reconstructs the DSSF from the predicted parameters, providing a rapid self-consistency check and a visualization of the predicted response. When interactions are strong, networks trained on LSWT and THL spectra infer markedly different parameters. Analysis of the Fisher information matrix shows that the measurement protocol, including which spin-correlation components are resolved and the momentum cut, determines which couplings can be identified. Combining machine learning with fast many- body theory is therefore essential for quantitative Hamiltonian inference from scattering data.

title: Altermagnetic magnon splitting in hematite: from bulk g-wave to planar i-wave
summary: Hematite is an insulating iron oxide with both a collinear antiferromagnetic and a weakly ferromagnetic phase with intriguing properties, such as long-range spin transport distances, that make it promising for spintronics applications. It has also been identified as a candidate for g-wave altermagnetism. Here, we present the results of fully relativistic ab initio calculations of the magnon properties of hematite, with a focus on altermagnetic effects. We quantitatively evaluate both the anisotropic and altermagnetic magnon band splitting as well as the magnon lifetimes. We show that dipolar interactions lead to a sizeable non-altermagnetic splitting and a hybridisation between opposite-chirality magnons resulting in a strong reduction of the spin expectation value of magnons close to the Γ point and around nodal planes, even in the collinear out-of-plane phase. Both the frequencies and the lifetimes have a large altermagnetic splitting in the $k_z = 0$ plane, which is characteristic of hematite and not generally expected for g-wave altermagnets. We compare our results to the prototypical, hexagonal g-wave altermagnet manganese telluride, which has four symmetry-protected nodal planes, whereas the fourth nodal surface in hematite is not completely fixed by symmetry. We derive implicit analytical expressions for this surface and discuss how it arises from a combination of rotational and translational symmetry, which leads to a transition to i-wave symmetry at the Brillouin zone boundary. The example of hematite reveals the trigonal altermagnets as a special case where the splitting function exhibits both bulk (g-wave) and planar (i-wave) components, and shows that the point symmetries alone are not sufficient to capture the full symmetry-determined behaviour of the splitting function.

title: Symmetry-resolved spectroscopy of truncation-induced perturbations in loop tensor network renormalization of the six-vertex model
summary: Tensor network renormalization at finite bond dimension $χ$ introduces truncation errors that are amplified by the renormalization-group (RG) flow. For loop tensor network renormalization (LoopTNR) on the $c=1$ critical line of the six-vertex model, with Luttinger parameter $K$, we identify these errors operator by operator from symmetry-resolved transfer-matrix spectra and conformal perturbation theory. With $O(2)$ symmetry imposed, the dominant error is the dimerization operator, which is allowed because LoopTNR breaks one-site translation. With less symmetry it is the $U(1)$ current or a charge-two vertex operator. The growth of the dimerization per RG step and a parameter-free ratio of its amplitudes agree with conformal perturbation theory to within a few percent. The parameter $K$ drifts slowly, owing to a weak marginal error and to the running induced by the dimerization. A larger $χ$ lowers the initial amplitude of the error for $0.75\le K\le 1.5$ but changes neither the operator nor its growth rate.

title: Weakly coordinating anions and solvents break the conductivity-transference-solvation tradeoff
comment: 12 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to Science. Under review
summary: Lithium-metal batteries promise high energy density, but common electrolytes trade ionic conductivity against the share of current carried by lithium ions and against how strongly solvent binds those ions. We show that simultaneously weakening both interactions of the lithium ion, with solvent and with anion, relaxes this trade-off. Thus, a weakly coordinating perfluorinated alkoxyaluminate salt in liquefied fluoromethane conducts 39.2 mS cm$^{-1}$ at 25 $^\circ$C while maintaining a lithium-ion transference number of 0.71. Molecular dynamics simulations further reveal that the anion prevents persistent ion aggregation and lowers the salt's dissociation penalty. Consistent with these properties, nickel-rich cathode/lithium-metal anode full cells charge at 10C at room temperature and at 2C at $-40$ $^\circ$C. We advance coordination strength as a design axis for future energy storage devices.

title: Momentum-space quantum Monte Carlo for twisted bilayer graphene: Interaction effects in the presence of remote bands
summary: Twisted bilayer graphene hosts strong correlation effects within topological flat bands separated from remote dispersive bands. This separation motivates projection onto the central bands, which greatly reduces the computational complexity of many-body calculations, including momentum-space quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations. However, the interaction-induced Mott gap obtained in the projected model can be comparable to the noninteracting flat--remote band separation, raising the question of whether the projection remains valid. Here, we extend momentum-space QMC to explicitly include remote BM bands within a broad energy window at charge neutrality. We find that the projected description remains reliable over a broad parameter regime, up to $u_0/u_1\lesssim0.9$: the projected and remote-band calculations yield similar low-energy electron and trion spectra, and the Kramers intervalley-coherent ground state remains stable. In particular, the Dirac trion remains robust in the finite-temperature normal state when remote bands are included. Near the band-touching limit $u_0=u_1$, remote-band electrons acquire substantial low-energy spectral weight, accompanied by suppression of the trion weight and loss of the Kramers intervalley-coherent state. Our findings establish the broad validity of flat-band projection while reconciling the projected and THF viewpoints by identifying the near-band-touching regime in which explicit remote-band degrees of freedom become essential.

title: Origin and hole-density dependence of the intrinsic spin Hall conductivity in inorganic halide perovskites
comment: The manuscript is 30 pages in total, including the Supporting Information. The main text is 20 pages with 4 figures and 2 tables, and the Supporting Information is 10 pages with 6 figures and 6 tables
summary: Metal halide perovskites have spin-orbit coupling among the strongest in semiconductors, yet whether their centrosymmetric bulk phases can convert charge current into spin current, and what controls the response, is unknown. Here we identify, from first-principles calculations on the four all-inorganic compounds CsBX3 (B = Pb, Sn; X = Br, I), the factors that govern their intrinsic spin Hall conductivity. The conductivity arises from the spin Berry curvature of the spin-orbit-split halide-p bands, 1.1-2.6 eV below the valence band maximum, and exceeds that of III-V and group-IV semiconductors when the Fermi level lies inside them. Because the valence band maximum is an s-p singlet, shifted only in second order, these contributions cancel in the undoped compounds, which respond like conventional semiconductors. With hole doping the response recovers, and at densities reachable by electric double-layer gating CsPbI3 attains the spin Hall conductivity of p-GaAs. The response is therefore determined by the position of the halide-p bands relative to the valence band maximum, not by the atomic spin-orbit constant, a criterion that applies to any semiconductor with an orbital-singlet band edge. These results point to CsPbI3 as a candidate gate-controlled source of spin current for perovskite spin-orbit torque devices.

title: Interaction-driven phase transition between bosonic Moore-Read and Laughlin states in a multiple flat-band model
summary: Lattice models with multiple nearly flat bands provide additional degrees of freedom for realizing fractional Chern insulators and studying competition between distinct topological orders. Here we report numerical evidence for the interaction-driven phase transition between the non-Abelian and Abelian topologically ordered states at fixed filling factor in a multiple flat-band lattice model. We construct a six-site Kekulé lattice model with two low-energy nearly flat bands whose Chern numbers are $1$ and $0$, respectively. At one boson per unit cell (a site filling of $\frac{1}{6}$), the weak two-body repulsion favors a Moore-Read state predominantly occupying the lowest band, whereas stronger repulsion favors a Laughlin-like state with substantial occupations of both lower bands. We identify the two states by the low-energy spectra, particle entanglement spectra, and many-body Chern numbers, using the real-space and band-projected exact diagonalization, supplemented by infinite density-matrix renormalization group calculations. Our results provide alternative platform to study the quantum phase transition of distinct topological orders beyond the conventional multilayer systems.

title: Scattering Circular Dichroism from Spatially Modulated Anisotropic Magnetic Dipoles in BiFeO$_3$
summary: Antiferromagnets with broken time-reversal symmetry, including altermagnets, have attracted growing interest because they can exhibit ferromagnet-like responses, such as the anomalous Hall effect and magneto-optical effects, despite their compensated spin structures. Such time-reversal symmetry breaking is characterized by ferroic time-reversal-odd multipoles, distinct from the conventional spin and orbital moments. Among them, the anisotropic magnetic dipole (AMD), which reflects the local orbital anisotropy, shares the symmetry of magnetization and can have a ferroic component even when the spin moments cancel. AMD responses have thus far been identified primarily in antiferromagnets with unit-cell magnetic periodicity, whereas spatially modulated AMDs in long-wavelength magnetic textures remain unexplored. Here, we report resonant soft x-ray small-angle scattering measurements on the antiferromagnetic spin cycloid of the multiferroic BiFeO$_3$. We observe pronounced circular dichroism in the resonant scattering intensity, i.e., scattering circular dichroism, which is not expected from the established cycloidal and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya-interaction-induced sinusoidal spin structures. We show that the staggered rotation of the FeO$_6$ octahedra gives rise to ferroic AMD components despite the antiparallel spin alignment. As the local magnetic symmetry varies with the cycloidal phase, these AMDs are spatially modulated and produce the dichroism through interference with the sinusoidal spin component. Our findings demonstrate that long-wavelength antiferromagnetic textures can host spatially modulated AMDs, opening new avenues for exploring hidden multipole textures in magnetic and multiferroic materials.

title: Current-driven resistive switching in high-field heavy fermion metal UTe2
summary: In UTe$_2$, superconductivity persists up to 70 T for fields tilted by roughly 20-40° from the b axis toward c. Its normal state is a field-polarized (FP) state, which emerges above a first-order metamagnetic transition when the field component along b exceeds $\sim$35 T. Despite being the parent of this high-field superconductivity, the FP state remains poorly understood, including whether it shares underlying physics with the low-field paramagnetic (PM) state from which it is abruptly separated. Using microstructures fabricated by focused ion beam, we reach current densities of 30-60 kA/cm2 and observe a current-induced high-resistivity state in both the PM and FP regimes over a wide range of field angles in the bc plane. Above a critical current density of order 10 kA/cm2, the resistivity sharply rises to values comparable to those near the critical end point of the metamagnetic transition. The critical current density increases with temperature, opposite to the trend expected from Joule heating, ruling out a thermal origin. The emergence of the same instability on both sides of the metamagnetic transition reveals an unexpected commonality between the FP and PM states. More broadly, the observation of a current-induced transition in a heavy-fermion metal exposes the multitude of nearby electronic states in correlated electron systems and shows that electric current, like magnetic field and pressure, can switch between them.

title: AdsNet: A Graph Neural Network for Direct Adsorption Energy Prediction
comment: 24 pages, 6 figures, 1 table; includes Supplementary Information (4 pages, 2 tables). AdsNet is MIT-licensed. Code: https://github.com/changzhiai/AdsNet - Documentation: https://adsnet.readthedocs.io - Dataset (AdsTraj): https://huggingface.co/datasets/changzhiai/AdsTraj - Model weights: https://huggingface.co/changzhiai/adsnet-models
summary: Fast and accurate prediction of adsorption energies is critical for high-throughput computational catalyst screening, existing methods compromise either on evaluation speed (full-graph machine learning potentials) or geometric sensitivity (coordination-based models like the alpha-scheme). Here, we present AdsNet, an equivariant graph neural network that directly predicts adsorption energies in a single forward pass, which operates on a local graph restricted only to adsorbate atoms and its immediate surface neighbors within a cutoff radius. This local graph formulation decouples computational complexity from total system size while encoding continuous geometric features (interatomic distances and directional vectors) enabling sensitivity to subtle variations in local bonding environments. AdsNet adopts a message-passing architecture with scalar and vector node features over multiple interaction layers. Trained on AdsTraj, a dataset of 33,920 density functional theory (DFT) calculated structures spanning 26 transition metals and 6 adsorbates (H*, C*, O*, CO*, OH*, HOCO*), the model achieves an adsorption energy root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.032 eV and a force RMSE of 0.047 eV/A. Analytic forces obtained via automatic differentiation enable structure relaxation through a projected gradient descent algorithm with adaptive line search, eliminating entire geometry optimizations. Additionally, AdsNet uniquely decomposes predicted adsorption energies into contributions from individual atoms within the local adsorbate graph - an interpretability feature unattainable with conventional machine-learning potentials. AdsNet thus establishes an accurate, highly efficient, and interpretable framework for large-scale adsorption energy prediction and local interface relaxation across various material surfaces.

title: Fast extraction of universal data from temporal spectrum: Applications to Haagerup CFT and monopole scattering
comment: 10 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables; includes Supplemental Material
summary: Extracting precise universal data on conformal field theory (CFT) on the lattice traditionally requires large-scale simulations of the ground states and excitations of critical systems. Here, we propose an alternative accurate and fast algorithm, where we read off the CFT spectrum from the transfer matrix spectrum of an infinite matrix product state after a short imaginary-time evolution. We apply this method to extract the charge-resolved spectrum of a Haagerup CFT to higher levels and obtain a central charge $c = 2.137(27)$. Moreover, we show that the Maldacena--Ludwig monopole boundary can be realized as the ground state of the Fidkowski--Kitaev Hamiltonian after space-time rotation.

title: Thermally driven multiple sliding states and avalanche dynamics in rhombohedral Pb(TaSe2)2 nanoflakes
summary: Interlayer sliding in van der Waals materials offers a promising route to control functional properties, yet a comprehensive understanding of the complex collective domain dynamics governing these transitions remains challenging. Here, we investigate thermally driven sliding dynamics in Pb(TaSe2)2 nanoflakes, incorporating transport and atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) measurements. Reducing the flake thickness induces multiple stepwise resistance jumps with enhanced hysteresis, corresponding to transitions between stacking domains accompanied by ripplocations. Statistical analysis of the jumps reveals collective avalanche behavior of domain dynamics with universal power-law scaling, quantifying the domain motion. Harnessing these features, we demonstrate controllable, non-volatile multi-level resistive switching, including write/erase operations, via thermal cycling. These findings provide valuable insights into the sliding dynamics for various 2D materials, with significant implications for the development of slidetronics devices.

title: Phase diagram of the attractive lattice Fermi polaron and the instability of Nagaoka ferromagnetism
summary: On the square lattice, the attractive polaron competes not only with the dimeron but also with Yang's $η$ dimer, an exact eigenstate that maps onto the Nagaoka ferromagnet. With two-particle--hole Ansätze benchmarked by diagrammatic Monte Carlo, we find that the ground state evolves from polaron to dimeron to $η$ dimer at low filling, and, beyond a triple point, directly from polaron to $η$ dimer. Above 25\% filling it stays a polaron. As the $η$ dimer is exact, its boundary is a rigorous instability criterion for Nagaoka ferromagnetism, sharper than the previous best and logarithmic at low filling.

title: Intelligent Imaging of Thermal Transport in Nanostructures
summary: The ability to measure thermal properties and visualize heat transport processes with high spatial resolution is becoming increasingly important for materials discovery, next-generation electronics, and advanced manufacturing. As critical dimensions and architectures of novel materials and high performance electronics shrink and become more heterogeneous, thermal transport is no longer governed by bulk material properties alone, but by local variations in microstructure, such as interfaces and defects, while the operating conditions can also play a role. With the development of non-contact pump-probe thermoreflectance techniques, specific heat, thermal conductivity, and interface conductance can be mapped either through wide-field thermos-reflectance images or by scanning technique. However, key challenges remain such as the balance between imaging throughput and measurement accuracy, the extraction of multiple parameters with high confidence, and non-intrusive subsurface characterization, etc. This Review highlights recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI)-assistance in high-throughput data processing, visualizing interfacial thermal transport, and nonintrusive subsurface analysis, and offers outlooks for future research directions such as spectral mapping of heat carriers, three-dimensional property mapping, and AI-agentic experimental designs. We anticipate this Review will motivate future efforts in combining AI with experimental techniques to achieve unprecedented capabilities for thermal characterization of nanoscale materials and device characterization, facilitating materials discovery and electronics revolution.

title: Quantum Metric Control of Topological Superconductivity and Incommensurate Charge Density Wave in an Interacting Lieb-Kitaev Chain Model
summary: We study an interacting spinless Lieb-Kitaev chain model in the nearly flat-band regime, motivated by the recent observation that Majorana zero modes in the noninteracting Lieb-Kitaev system inherit two decay modes: an ordinary Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) length and a longer geometric length controlled by the quantum metric. By tuning both the interaction strength and quantum metric, we identify a topological superconducting (TSC) phase, an incommensurate charge-density-wave (ICDW)phase, and a commensurate charge-density-wave (CDW) phase. Inside the TSC phase, the QML is enhanced when increasing the interactions. In the ICDW phase, the interactions are modulated by quantum metric to generate an effective chemical potential, leading to a discontinuous incommensurate-to-commensurate (IC-C) transition. We verify these phases and conclusions using low energy effective theory and density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations.

title: Molecular Dynamics Simulation of the Solidification of AlCoCuFeNi High-Entropy Alloy Nanowire
summary: Molecular dynamics simulation of the solidification behavior of an AlCoCuFeNi high-entropy alloy nanowire was performed using an embedded atom model potential at cooling rates of 10^11, 10^12, and 10^13 K/s. Periodic boundary conditions were applied along the nanowire axis to model an effectively infinite nanowire. The crystallization process was characterized through the temperature dependence of the potential energy. Structural evolution was analyzed using adaptive common-neighbor analysis (CNA) and radial distribution functions (RDF). The results show that the final structure changes from amorphous to crystalline with decreasing cooling rate, demonstrating the strong influence of cooling conditions on phase formation in nanoscale high-entropy alloy systems.

title: Nonstandard quantum statistics for strongly correlated systems: Superexclusion in momentum space and comparison with exact results
summary: We analyze in detail nonstandard statistics for strongly correlated fermions, which comprise the statistical spin liquid (SSL) and model non-Fermi liquid (NFL) cases. Both of those cases are based on the total exclusion of local doubly occupancies ($the~superexclusion$) either in real space (SSL case) or in reciprocal ($\mathbf{k}$) space (NFL). The results obtained on a purely physical ground are supplemented with the exact analysis of those coming from microscopic Hubbard-like model in $\mathbf{k}$ space. Specifically, we discuss the transmutation of those statistics to that of localized magnetic moments, as well as the transformation of the Fermi liquid into a strongly correlated fermionic liquid or Mott insulating state; the latter taking place for the half-filled-band situation. The role of exclusion of double occupancies in either real or reciprocal space in the appearance of the correlated phase is stressed. Conclusions concerning the universal features of the models, independence of either the real- or $\mathbf{k}$-space representation, are also discussed. One of those is the boson to fermion statistics transmutation which in the limit of strong repulsive interboson interaction leads to the particle localization instead to the Bose-Einstein condensation.

title: Precise experimental investigation of the reflection properties caused by s-polarized evanescent waves and the Casimir puzzle
comment: 19 pages, 8 figures; accepted for publication in Phys. Rev. A
summary: We report a high-precision experiment on measuring the low-frequency magnetic field reflected from a metallic plate. This experiment is designed to give insight into why theoretical predictions of the fundamental Lifshitz theory using the standard response function to the electromagnetic waves are in contradiction with the data of numerous precision measurements of the Casimir force (the Casimir puzzle). To attain these ends, we measured the magnitude and phase of the lateral component of the magnetic field produced by an oscillating magnetic dipole and reflected from a metallic plate. These quantities are completely determined by the evanescent waves with the transverse electric (s) polarization. The obtained measurement data are compared with theoretical predictions using the standard Drude response function of the metal to the low-frequency electromagnetic waves. It is shown that there are both quantitative and qualitative disagreements with these predictions, so that in the region of low-frequency s-polarized evanescent waves the Drude response function is excluded by the data. Keeping in mind that just the s-polarized evanescent waves are responsible for the Casimir puzzle, our results highlight the causes for its emergence. It is emphasized that, in addition to the Casimir effect, searching for the adequate nonlocal response functions of metals to the evanescent waves is of utmost significance for many areas of physics as near-field optical microscopy, nanophotonics, surface plasmon polaritons, radiative heat transfer, and others.

title: Magnon high-harmonic generation by nonlinearities of spin torque driven by phonon-mediated crossing of many-body energy levels of bright and dark excitons
summary: Recent intense experimental focus on CrSBr, a two-dimensional (2D) antiferromagnetic semiconductor, has revealed numerous surprises in its response to ultrafast optical drive. We demonstrate that a single microscopic mechanism accounts for two of them---high-harmonic generation of magnons and persistence of magnon oscillations over \mbox{$\sim 1$ ns} time scale that is much longer than the femtosecond laser pulse (fsLP) pump duration. This mechanism arises from an unusually complex interplay of four different fundamental quasiparticles of condensed matter physics: magnons, optically bright and dark excitons, and phonons. By viewing magnons as the system and the other three quasiparticles as a quantum many-body bath, we derive an extended Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (eLLG) equation. Its new term generated by the bath is spatially nonlocal and time-dependent, as well as strongly {\em nonlinear} when the {\em crossing of many-body energy levels} of bright and dark excitons occurs via phonon mediation. It also resembles the so-called field-like spin-transfer torque (STT) in spintronics, but STT is driven there with current pulses, so it explains the microscopic origin of the recently experimentally conjectured {\em excitonic STT}. Since dark excitons supply energy to magnons long after the fsLP is switched off, such a reservoir opens avenues for its engineering and applications in optospintronics and optomagnonics, neuromorphic computing, and quantum transduction.

title: momipy: A time-resolved momentum microscopy data analysis workflow
summary: Photoemission momentum microscopy is an emerging approach to photoelectron spectroscopy that is transforming electronic band structure mapping at both laboratory-based and large-scale facilities. Its extension to time-resolved measurements has recently enabled major advances, ranging from the femtosecond imaging of exciton wavefunctions to dark-field photoelectron microscopy of light-induced dynamics and strong light-matter interactions. However, the rapid acquisition of high-dimensional data sets (including electron in-plane momenta $k_x$ and $k_y$, kinetic energy $E_\mathrm{kin}$, time $Δt$, and more) poses substantial challenges for data handling and analysis. A typical workflow encompasses data acquisition, exploratory visualization, calibration and targeted feature extraction, with data management ideally guided by FAIR principles. Here, we present momipy, a Python package that streamlines the momentum microscopy data analysis workflow efficiently and at low computational cost. Among other features, momipy provides interactive 4D data visualization, energy and momentum calibration, space-charge correction, and a broad selection of multidimensional data analysis routines, including binning, momentum-map extraction and time-, energy- and momentum-resolved model fitting. momipy is accompanied by a selection of interactive example scripts, supporting adoption of momipy by both experienced researchers and users new to momentum microscopy.

title: Scalable Simulation of Strongly Correlated Fermions with Neural Gaussian Tensor Networks
summary: Accurate simulations of strongly correlated electrons remain a central challenge in computational physics. We introduce neural-network Gaussian projected entangled-pair states (NN-GPEPS), which exploit the locally-entangled subspace of Gaussian states to give an architecture more compatible with modern neural networks and an exact contraction cost of $O(N^{3/2})$ on two-dimensional lattices. For the Hubbard model at $U/t=8$ and $1/8$ hole doping, we obtain state-of-the-art variational energies in large lattices of up to 1024 sites. These results demonstrate an accurate approach to strongly correlated fermions by connecting neural networks with Gaussian tensor networks.

title: Ab-initio study of magnetic interaction in RNiO2: role of rare-earth size and epitaxial strain
summary: In this paper we present a systematic first-principles investigation of the structure and nearest-neighbor magnetic exchange interactions in the infinite-layer RNiO2 thin-film series (R = La-Lu), under the constrain of different substrates. Density functional theory calculations are first employed to optimize the crystal structures, while CAS+DDCI correlated wave-function calculations were used for the determination of the magnetic exchanges. This methodology allows to obtain magnetic interactions in good agreement with RIXS experimental estimations. In the pristine case, our results confirm that the structure of RNiO2 (except for R = La and Ce) adopts the I4/mcm space group, characterized by an out-of-plane rotation of the NiO4 plaquettes. This result remains valid under substrate constrains, even if compressive strain reduces the amplitude of the rotational distortion and leads to an enhancement of the magnetic exchange interaction relative to the pristine structures. The latter are found to depend sensitively on both the rare-earth ionic radius and the applied epitaxial strain. These results highlight the role of structural distortions and substrate-induced strain in tuning magnetic interactions in infinite-layer nickelates.

title: Large transformation strain of $\mathrm{Ni}_{50}\mathrm{Fe}_{23}\mathrm{Ga}_{27}$ microwires produced by the Taylor-Ulitovsky method
summary: The martensitic transformation and associated tensile strain of $\mathrm{Ni}_{50}\mathrm{Fe}_{23}\mathrm{Ga}_{27}$ microwires produced by the Taylor--Ulitovsky method were investigated using thermomechanical analysis, electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD), and in-situ tensile X-ray diffraction (XRD). EBSD mapping at room temperature reveals cubic austenite in a nonstrained part of the microwire and tetragonal martensite in the strained part. Both EBSD and XRD show that both austenite and martensite have $[001]$ directions approximately parallel to the wire axis. The axial transformation strain calculated from the measured lattice parameters is approximately $15.4\%$. Thermal cycling under constant stresses of $20\text{--}100~\mathrm{MPa}$ reveals experimental transformation strains of $13.2\text{--}14.0\%$. Increasing tensile stress raises the transformation temperatures, with a stress--temperature slope of approximately $1.52~\mathrm{MPa}/^\circ\mathrm{C}$, comparable to that reported for $[001]$-oriented $\mathrm{Ni\text{--}Fe\text{--}Ga}$ single crystals. Overall, the observations confirm that the large macroscopic strain of up to $14.0\%$ relates to the nearly complete martensitic transformation in the microwire.

title: Thermal investigation of buffer and transition layers in AlGaN HEMT stacks
summary: In this work, we investigate thermal transport in a set of thin-film layers used in modern HEMT designs. Our theoretical analysis employs three phonon-transport models of increasing sophistication, ranging from a relatively simple Debye-approximation model to a first-principles framework that incorporates Density Functional Theory (DFT)-derived harmonic and anharmonic phonon properties. To describe ternary semiconductors, alloy scattering is also considered, and to account for the properties of non-ideal, polycrystalline thin films, scattering at grain and film boundaries is taken into account. For modeling the specific samples at hand, the latter are fitted to thermal conductivity data measured with Time-Domain Thermoreflectance (TDTR). Overall, we find that the first-principles model performs best and produces the most physically consistent results. Special emphasis is placed on establishing a reliable procedure for determining intrinsic transport properties dominated by Umklapp scattering. Building on these, it is then possible to systematically add additional scattering terms to the models and assess how model-inherent factors, such as the treatment of scattering rates or the description of the phonon dispersion, affect model accuracy and overall predictive capabilities.

title: Alloying effects on the interface cohesion of grain boundaries in the Ni--Fe--Cr system
summary: Grain boundaries (GBs) in polycrystalline Ni-based alloys strongly influence mechanical strength and fracture behavior, yet the effect of alloying elements such as Fe and Cr on GB cohesion remains difficult to quantify systematically. Using density functional theory (DFT), we compute rigid-body separation (RBS) curves for six symmetric-tilt Ni GBs, extracting the work of separation $W_{\mathrm{sep}}$ and maximum traction $σ_{\max}$ via the universal binding energy relation (UBER). We find that substitution of Cr or Fe into the GB plane increases both quantities relative to pure Ni GBs. To overcome the size limitations of DFT, we compare several machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) foundation models against the DFT dataset and identify a model achieving quantitative agreement with DFT for $W_{\mathrm{sep}}$ and $σ_{\max}$. This MLIP enables systematic sampling of alloying configurations at finer concentration steps. We show that alloying-induced changes in GB cohesion depend on both, element type and local structures, revealing trends that are inaccessible with DFT alone. Extending the analysis to a ternary $\mathrm{Ni}_{56}\mathrm{Fe}_{20}\mathrm{Cr}_{24}$ composition, inspired by the principal constituents of the widely used commercial Alloy 718, shows that the binary trends provide a useful basis for interpreting the combined effect of both substitutes, while explicit ternary calculations are required to capture their interplay quantitatively. Together, these results provide a validated workflow for quantifying the effect of alloying elements on GB cohesion in multicomponent alloys. The resulting values may serve as input for continuum-scale fracture models, paving the way toward atomistically informed multiscale modeling.

title: Multicharged Kramers-Weyl Fermions, Quantum Geometric Hall Responses and de Haas-van Alphen Oscillations in WAl$_2$
summary: Quantum geometry of Bloch wave functions and crystalline symmetries play a central role in condensed matter physics, shaping the electronic topology and physical responses of solids. In particular, Kramers-Weyl fermions, spin-split Fermi surfaces probed through quantum oscillations and quantum geometric nonlinear Hall and intrinsic spin Hall responses have garnered significant attention. Despite progress in understanding these phenomena individually, their coexistence with topological surface states, Fermi arcs and chirality dependent quantum geometric transport remains scarce, as pronounced responses involve suitable symmetries, SOC and Fermi surface geometry. Here, we explore this synergy in experimentally synthesized WAl$_2$, considering both structural enantiomers using first-principles calculations and symmetry analysis. We observed twelve Kramers-Weyl (KW) crossings with quantized chiral charges $|C|=1$ and $|C|=3$, accompanied by nontrivial surface states and Fermi arcs. The pronounced metallic character gives rise to six Fermi surface sheets exhibiting antisymmetric SOC, with distinct extremal orbits and candidate spin-split pairs resolved through calculated de Haas-van Alphen (dHvA) quantum oscillations. The electronic structure also exhibits large intrinsic Berry curvature dipole (BCD) arising from the asymmetric distribution of Berry curvature, giving rise to a nonlinear Hall response. The opposite structural handedness of the two enantiomers reverses the chiralities and BCD, reversing the direction of Fermi arcs and nonlinear Hall current. BCD attains $|D_{zz}|\approx0.338$, yielding nonlinear Hall current densities $|j_x|\approx5.04\times10^{10}~\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$ and $|j_y|\approx2.52\times10^{10}~\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$. We observe enhanced SHC associated with triply charged KW point at $Γ$, suggesting role of higher Chern number in the SHC.

title: Lattice dynamics study of (Bi1-xSbx)2Te3 compounds: Comparative compositional study of force constants and Grüneisen parameters
summary: We performed a comprehensive Raman spectroscopy study of (Bi1-xSbx)2Te3 (BST-x) compounds, with varying Sb concentration, under ambient and high-pressure conditions. At ambient conditions, the frequency of all observed Raman-active modes (E1g, A11g, E2g, A21g) is blue-shifting with increasing Sb concentration, albeit with varying concentration-dependent rate. Based on these results, we calculated the relative force constants as a function of Sb concentration using a harmonic approximation, which shows a mode-dependent variation. The force constants for the lower frequency Raman modes (E1 g and A11g) remain almost composition-independent, while for the higher-frequency ones a profound softening (E2g) or stiffening (A21g) was determined. From the Raman spectroscopy measurements under high-pressure conditions, the corresponding Grüneisen parameters for the three observed Raman-active modes (A11g, E2g, A21g) as a function of composition were determined by combining them with the previously reported Equation of States and the corresponding bulk modulus B0 of the ambient-conditions R-3m phase. The average Grüneisen parameter exhibits a clear maximum for BST-07. Based on Slack's equation, these results are directly related to the optimal ZT values for this composition. Our study provides a solid framework for connecting composition, lattice dynamics, and thermal-transport behaviour, towards establishing the microscopic origin of thermoelectric optimization in BST compounds.

title: Reward misalignment as an opportunity for materials discovery
comment: 33 pages (15 pages main text and 18 pages Supplementary Information), 4 figures
summary: Reward misalignment is usually regarded as a failure of artificial intelligence. In materials discovery with generative AI models, however, disagreement between predefined rewards and expert judgment may reveal materials that the rewards overlook. We investigate this possibility using electronic flat bands as a prime example. Experts mostly agree with a numerical bandwidth score, but their disagreements are systematic and cannot be explained by an estimated 5% rate of mistaken labels. We learn the experts' preferences from pairwise comparisons and use them to guide a crystal diffusion model. The learned preferences and numerical score agree on the flattest bands but diverge elsewhere. For example, the preferences favor KCo2As2 and CoGa, reported compounds with partially flat bands that the score would discard. The framework also extends to synthesizability and phonon properties. Our findings suggest that reward misalignment can expose opportunities for materials discovery beyond what fixed rewards are designed to find.

title: Unusual increase in electrical and thermal conductivity of severely deformed CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy: Roles of disordering and nanostructuring in electron and phonon transport
summary: This work investigates how defect engineering and nanostructuring via severe plastic deformation influence electrical and thermal transport in the high-entropy alloy CrMnFeCoNi. High-pressure torsion (HPT) for up to N = 4 turns produces a hierarchical defect structure, including deformation twins at low strains, dislocations and Lomer-Cottrell locks at intermediate strains, and a high fraction of high-angle grain boundaries at large strains. While hardness naturally increases and saturates at ~520 Hv, both electrical and thermal conductivity exhibit an unusual increase upon HPT processing (from 0.953 MS m-1 and 10.3 W m-1 K-1 after homogenization to 1.003 +- 0.005 MS m-1 and 14.4 W m-1 K-1 after N = 4). Analysis based on the Wiedemann-Franz law indicates a modest increase in electron transport (~5%) and a significant increase in phonon transport (~100%) after HPT processing. The phonon mean free path remains small on the order of 0.6-1.1 nm, and comparison with the Cahill-Pohl model shows that heat transport occurs near the minimum thermal conductivity limit, where vibrational modes are strongly scattered. This suggests that the enhancement in thermal transport is not governed by conventional defect scattering, but it is hypothesized that modifications in atomic-scale disorder, such as deformation-induced short-range ordering, are responsible for this unusual behavior. Specific heat capacity increases after HPT, consistent with stored defect energy. The linear thermal expansion exhibits a non-monotonic behavior, decreasing initially due to internal stresses and relaxation effects, and increasing at higher strains due to grain boundary-induced anharmonicity. These findings highlight the complex interplay between defects, atomic-scale disorder, and nanostructure in governing the electrical and thermal properties of severely deformed high-entropy alloys via electron and phonon scattering.

title: Perfumer: A Large Language Model-based Agentic Framework Accelerating Structural Relaxation and Electronic Band Prediction for First-Principle Calculation
summary: First-principles structural relaxation and band calculations require substantial computation and expertise. Here we present Perfumer, a large language model-based agentic framework that couples Quantum ESPRESSO with two predictive models. Across tested structures, pre-relaxation with Perfumer-relax model followed by QE refinement yielded a 2.75-fold overall speedup over QE alone. Perfumer-band model combines a periodic graph neural network with a latent Hermitian spectral head returns 12 band energies at any requested wavevector, preserving reciprocal lattice periodicity and time-reversal symmetry without constructing Hamiltonian. Trained on 125,153 self-curated band structures, Perfumer-band model reaches a median per-material mean absolute error of 0.157 eV on 2,607 test materials, including lanthanide, actinide and magnetic compounds, from held-out composition families spanning 85 elements, taking about 97 ms per material on two consumer CPU cores. The agent turns natural-language requests into relaxation-to-band workflows, from a single uploaded structure to automatically constructed new candidates and returns predicted properties.

title: Two distinct notions of speed in antiferromagnets
summary: The terahertz resonance frequencies of antiferromagnets characterize their precessional dynamics but do not necessarily imply faster laser-induced quenching of magnetic order. Here, we investigate the distinct roles of magnetic compensation and electronic scattering phase space by comparing ultrafast demagnetization in the antiferromagnetic charge-transfer insulator NiO, the metallic antiferromagnet Mn2Au, and a ferromagnetic Ni reference. The extracted response in Mn2Au is approximately four times faster than in NiO and substantially faster than in Ni. These observations are consistent with exchange-mediated scattering between antiparallel sublattices enabling rapid loss of antiferromagnetic order without requiring net angular-momentum transfer to an external reservoir, provided sufficient electronic scattering phase space is available. In insulating NiO, restricted electronic scattering channels reduces the ultrafast response. Our results distinguish ultrafast demagnetization from exchange-enhanced precession and identify the interplay of spin-flip probability and electronic scattering rate as a key factor governing the nonequilibrium response of compensated magnets.

title: Constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Finite Element Model Updating: Closed-Form Hyperelastic Strain Energies from Heterogeneous Experiments
summary: Calibrating a hyperelastic constitutive model for a soft material traditionally poses two problems: an expert must choose its functional form, and several homogeneous tests must determine its parameters. Neural constitutive models solve the first, but either remain black boxes or draw on a library of candidate terms fixed in advance. Full-field measurements, such as those from digital image correlation (DIC), promise to solve the second, replacing those tests by a single heterogeneous one. Two gaps remain: flexibility during training with interpretability afterwards, and a way to train such a model on one heterogeneous test. Here we close both. We embed a constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold network (CKAN) in finite element model updating (FEMU) and train it by minimizing the mismatch between the predicted and the measured kinematic fields and reaction forces. Pruning and symbolic regression then reduce the trained network to a compact closed-form strain energy that satisfies every constitutive requirement. On perforated natural-rubber membranes, the CKANs reproduce the DIC displacement fields with median errors between one and two percent, and transfer to a hole pattern withheld from training. On a perforated silicone plate, a CKAN trained on one stretch profile at a single load reproduces that profile and the measured reaction force to within a few percent. On an aortic specimen inflated under pressure, an anisotropic CKAN predicts the inflated three-dimensional shape. The discovered closed-form energies match the CKANs they replace on the training data and can be compared directly with established models.

title: Emergent Fatigue Dynamics from Foundational Interatomic Potentials
summary: Foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials are trained on large, diverse DFT datasets, but their validation rests on equilibrium states, which does not guarantee correct emergent behavior in large-scale molecular dynamics. Where no direct experimental validation is available, comparisons to physically motivated potentials are valuable for drawing insight. We distinguish static properties, which are thermally accessible, from emergent properties, which require work from an external fatigue stress to drive rare events, and compare the potentials on both. An EAM potential and the NequIP foundational potential both agree closely with reference data for many near-equilibrium properties, but NequIP predicts an anomalously low intrinsic stacking fault energy ($\sim7$ times lower than EAM) and thus predicts far more plastic deformation under fatigue cycling of a nanoscale flaw modeled after the classical Griffith crack problem. Per-atom energy distributions after loading show that the two potentials differ most at energies far above what is thermally accessible. We also document memory-related crashes and silent extrapolation as practical concerns for practitioners of these foundational model forms.

title: Comparative First-Principles Study of the Physical Properties, Phonon-Mediated Superconductivity and Functional Potential of Technetium-Based Binary Borides TcB2, Tc2B and Tc3B
summary: Phonon-mediated superconductivity in binary transition-metal borides reflects a balance between the metal d-states, metal-boron bonding, and the lattice vibrations that couple to them. Here, we compare P6/mmm TcB2 at 20 GPa with I4/mcm Tc2B and P4/mmm Tc3B at 0 GPa within a first-principles framework. Their mechanical responses differ appreciably: TcB2 is the most rigid under its compressed condition, Tc2B shows the strongest tendency toward ductility, and Tc3B falls between the two. Despite these differences, all three phases remain metallic. The states at the Fermi level are dominated by Tc-4d character, although the extent of Tc-d/B-p mixing varies from one compound to another. Charge redistribution is more directional and B-centered in TcB2, but more delocalized around the Tc network in Tc2B and Tc3B. Inclusion of spin-orbit coupling leaves all three compounds metallic. The optical response remains metallic and electric field polarization dependent, with substantial visible reflectivity and strong ultraviolet absorption. Low-frequency Tc rich vibrations dominate the electron-phonon coupling (EPC). With μ* = 0.10, the Tc values of TcB2, Tc2B, and Tc3B are 24.92, 11.07, and 15.12 K, respectively. Although Tc3B exhibits a higher electronic density of states at the Fermi level, N(EF), TcB2 couples most strongly to EPC-active low-frequency modes, showing that the superconducting hierarchy depends on electronic-phonon matching rather than DOS magnitude alone.
